plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and lag/time-constant plus noise level at a mid input, which sets controller gain, integral time and filtering needed to reach 0.6 without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with lag hypothesis is right, y will rise gradually from ~0.23 by 0.1-0.3 over 10 s with 1-3 s lag, noisy +-0.02, staying well below 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and dead-zone upper bound and steady-state input needed for 0.6 by testing a second, higher amplitude that discriminates weak-gain vs high-threshold explanations for E1 flat response.
experiments.expected_observation: If higher-threshold positive-gain hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.19 for 1-3 s then rise 0.05-0.15 over remaining time, staying below ~0.4 with +/-0.02 noise; if y stays flat or decays, threshold is >0.8 or time constant >>8 s.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Natural drain/decay rate and time constant at u=0 and whether level holds, which sets steady-state pump needed for 0.6 and controller integral and drain compensation.
experiments.expected_observation: If drain hypothesis is right, y will fall gradually from ~0.37 by 0.05-0.15 over 15 s with no sustained rise, noisy +/-0.02, staying below 0.40; if y holds flat, drain is negligible and system is near-integrator.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Intermediate gain and threshold location between 0.5 and 0.8, which sets controller feedforward and gain needed to reach and hold 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If threshold-plus-lag hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.11 for 2-3 s then rise 0.08-0.15 to ~0.19-0.26 over 10 s with +/-0.02 noise, staying well below 0.6; if y stays flat or decays, threshold is >0.65 or gain is much lower.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-input gain magnitude and linearity versus saturation, which sets feedforward/steady-state u for 0.6 and safe controller gain to avoid overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If threshold-plus-lag hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.20 for 2-3 s then rise 0.10-0.18 to ~0.30-0.38 over 6 s with +/-0.02 noise, staying below 0.45; flat or much faster rise would falsify gain scaling.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain and equilibrium at elevated level 0.4-0.6 and whether u=0.8 can drive to target, which sets feedforward u for 0.6 and safe controller gain to avoid overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If threshold-plus-lag hypothesis is right, y will continue rising from ~0.39 by 0.08-0.14 to ~0.47-0.53 over 5 s with +/-0.02 noise and no flattening yet, staying below 0.60; if rise stalls to <0.05 then equilibrium for u=0.8 is near 0.40 and target 0.6 needs u>0.85.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-level steady-state gain and whether u=0.8 reaches 0.6, which sets feedforward holding input and safe controller gain to avoid steady-state error or overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If threshold-plus-lag hypothesis is right, y will continue rising from ~0.52 by 0.06-0.12 to ~0.58-0.64 over 4 s with +/-0.02 noise and no flattening yet, staying below 0.70; if rise stalls to <0.03 then equilibrium for u=0.8 is near 0.52 and target 0.6 needs higher u.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Natural drain rate and delay at operating level 0.6, which sets steady-state pump needed to hold 0.6 and controller integral/drain compensation to avoid overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If drain-plus-delay hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.61 for 2-3 s then fall 0.12-0.20 to ~0.42-0.52 over 8 s with +/-0.02 noise, staying below 0.65; if y holds flat, drain at high level is negligible and system is near-integrator.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Intermediate gain and steady-state holding input for 0.6 between 0.65 and 0.8, which sets feedforward and integral needed to reach and hold target without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If threshold-plus-lag hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.43 for 2-3 s then rise 0.06-0.12 to ~0.49-0.55 over 5 s with +/-0.02 noise, staying below 0.60; if rise stalls to <0.03 then u=0.7 net gain near 0.45 is insufficient and holding 0.6 needs >0.75, if rise >0.15 then holding needs <0.65.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Intermediate gain and holding input between 0.7 (insufficient) and 0.8 (sufficient) which sets feedforward for 0.6 and whether controller needs high integral authority for steep nonlinearity.
experiments.expected_observation: If threshold-plus-steep-gain hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.36 for 2-3 s delay then rise 0.05-0.10 to ~0.42-0.47 over remaining ~3 s with +/-0.02 noise, staying below 0.55; if y stays flat near 0.37 or decays like E9, then u=0.75 is still insufficient and holding 0.6 needs >=0.78-0.80.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Intermediate steady-state gain and holding input for 0.6 at operating level 0.46-0.58, discriminating whether u=0.75 equilibrium exceeds 0.6 or whether >=0.80 is needed, which sets feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If steep-gain hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.46 by 0.06-0.12 to ~0.52-0.58 over 5 s with +/-0.02 noise and no flattening, staying below 0.65; if rise stalls to <0.03 then equilibrium for u=0.75 is near 0.46 and holding 0.6 needs >=0.80.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Net flow and equilibrium at operating level for u=0.75: whether drift at ~0.56 is zero/positive (equilibrium >=0.60) or negative, which sets feedforward holding input for 0.6 and required integral authority given steep gain between 0.7 and 0.8.
experiments.expected_observation: If u=0.75 equilibrium >=0.60 hypothesis is right, y will hold/rise slowly from ~0.56 by 0.02-0.06 to ~0.58-0.62 over 3.5 s with +/-0.02 noise, staying in band and below 0.70; if y stays flat or falls, equilibrium for 0.75 is <=0.56 and holding 0.6 needs >=0.78-0.80.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive steady-state gain); u=0 does not raise level.
Step to u=0.5 from ~0.23 produces Delta-y > 0.05 within 10 s.
Response is not instantaneous: pure delay 2-4 s with dominant lag / time constant of order 8-15 s.

Effective dead-zone / low gain at low-mid input: u=0.5 equilibrates near 0.17-0.19, u=0.65 rises only at low level, u=0.7 fails to hold 0.43 and settles near 0.37, while u=0.75-0.9 produce clear rises, so response is strongly nonlinear with steep gain increase between 0.7 and 0.8.
At u=0 the level decays on its own toward near-zero with time constant of order 10 s, faster at higher level.
Steady-state y vs u is approximately linear over u in [0.2, 0.8].

Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.6 is in (0.7, 0.8], likely 0.73-0.80, because u=0.7 decays from 0.43 to ~0.37 while u=0.8 drives 0.39 to 0.61 with positive slope and u=0.75 drives 0.37 to 0.55 with positive slope and no flattening.
Sensor noise standard deviation is < 0.03 and zero-mean.
Equilibrium for u=0.8 exceeds 0.60, so target band is reachable without requiring u>0.9; u=0.8 held 5+4 s drove 0.39 to 0.61 with no flattening.

Equilibrium for u=0.7 is near 0.36-0.38 (E9 fell 0.43 to ~0.37 and flattened) while u=0.75 rises from same level and from 0.46 to 0.55 in 5 s, implying very steep steady-state gain between 0.7 and 0.8.
